item.title: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 Technical Report
item.description:
We are excited to announce the release of LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6, the latest upgrade to our open-source framework for audio-driven human video generation. Building upon LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5, 1.6 improves expressive naturalness, lip–audio synchronization, coordinated facial and body motion, and visual consistency during long-form generation. It also introduces comprehensive inference optimizations for faster and more efficient deployment.
Tasks: Talking Head Generation, Video generation
Code: https://github.com/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video

item.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
item.description:
Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.
Authors: Yunyang Ge, Weijie Kong, Ryan Xu, Yue Wu, Qi Tian, Jiangfeng Xiong, Bin Lin, Mingzhe Zheng, Shenghai Yuan, Zheyuan Liu, jianwei zhang, Li Yuan
Tasks: Streaming Video Understanding, Video generation
Code: https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/MovieRoll

item.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
item.description:
π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. We further present the data and training recipe underlying these capabilities, together with empirical studies of key design choices. Code and models are available at https://github.com/yyfz/Pi4.
Authors: Yifan WANG, Weiguang Zhao, Ni Yang, Haoyu Guo, Junting Dong, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen
Tasks: 2D Point Tracking, 3D Reconstruction, 3D Tracking, Camera Pose Estimation, Depth estimation, Video segmentation
Code: https://github.com/yyfz/Pi4

item.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
item.description:
Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. Therefore, we present ForceHarness, a harness that lets frozen models use force without demonstrations or finetuning. After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or joint torques alone, ForceHarness addresses the first challenge with self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event. To address the second challenge, a physics translation layer turns each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty as the tool result. To evaluate ForceHarness against expert force controllers and learned policies under identical conditions, we also build HiddenPhys, a seven-task MuJoCo benchmark with hidden physical variables. On a real arm without a wrist force sensor, ForceHarness raises the zero-shot success rate of GPT-6 Astra from 3.3% to 90.0%. In simulation, it adds 17.5 percentage points on the public ForceBench suite and 34.3 percentage points on HiddenPhys, surpassing force-aware policies trained on demonstrations on both benchmarks and matching hand-written expert controllers on HiddenPhys. Ablations further show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values.
Authors: Ke Sun, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Yike Zhang, Yanzhe Chen, Mike Zheng Shou
Tasks: Classic Reinforcement Learning, Continuous Control, Robotics
Code: https://github.com/showlab/ForceHarness

item.title: Multi-Branch Transformer
item.description:
Transformer language models are commonly scaled by making their blocks wider or stacking them deeper. In this work, we explore a complementary path: branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks. We introduce the Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT), which processes the input through shared initial layers, executes independently parameterized branches of sequential blocks in parallel, and fuses their outputs before shared final layers. At comparable training compute, we study three MBT variants: Wide-Shallow preserves block width, Narrow-Deep preserves sequential depth, and Balanced interpolates between them. In controlled pretraining experiments at four mixture-of-experts scales (0.8B to 2.1B total parameters), 2-branch Wide-Shallow MBTs consistently outperform sequential Transformers under matched parameter and training-compute budgets. Balanced MBTs improve further and retain comparable quality as the number of branches increases. To improve inference efficiency at long contexts, we introduce Joint-KV, which constructs a shared KV cache from branch representations at each depth. Our final recipe combines Balanced MBTs with Joint-KV, supported by an inference engine that exploits branch grouping and shared-cache reuse. Fitted scaling curves indicate that standard Transformers require up to 1.26x as much training body compute to match our final models' validation loss. These models reduce full-model KV-cache storage by up to 34% and deliver up to 51.4% higher decoding throughput on a single H200 GPU. Ablation studies show that branching yields gains beyond changes in width and depth, enables an effective KV-sharing strategy (Joint-KV), remains robust across fusion functions, and performs best in the middle layers. These findings show that branching offers a practical path for scaling language models toward both better modeling quality and faster inference.
Authors: Gaotang Li, Lingjie Chen, Chunyuan Deng, Zhiwei Xu, Hongzheng Chen, Christopher De Sa, Jingrui He, Yingheng Wang, Hanghang Tong
Tasks: Language Modeling, Long Context
Code: https://github.com/GaotangLi/Multi-Branch-Transformer

item.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
item.description:
Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.
Authors: Gene Chou, Guandao Yang, Fujun Luan, Lars Mescheder, Wei Dong, Stephan Richter, Vladlen Koltun
Tasks: Video generation
Code: https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-fastframes

item.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
item.description:
Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity in response to natural stimuli, but struggle to reveal which stimulus features drive those predictions. Here we introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), a method in which an LLM agent iteratively builds interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code, without gradient-based training (backpropagation). Without backpropagation to tune parameters, the agent must draw on its prior knowledge and reason over previous trials to hypothesize, hand-craft, and refine human-interpretable computations mirroring the workflow of a human scientist. LLM audits confirm the interpretability of the hand-crafted models. We first validate iWSP by tasking it with constructing transformers for canonical benchmarks such as arithmetic and sentiment classification, finding that LLM agents can successfully craft compact, accurate networks directly. Next, we apply iWSP to build neural encoding models across vision, language, and audition. In the visual cortex, iWSP outpredicts existing interpretable baselines, uncovers distinct computations across early/higher visual areas, and generalizes to unseen data. In language fMRI, iWSP surfaces a confound in the data and in auditory ECoG, it systematically discovers interpretable acoustic features that predict neural activity. Together, these results establish iWSP as a general paradigm for aligning high predictive performance with human-interpretable scientific discovery.
Authors: Yash Mehta, Chandan Singh, Weijia Xu, Richard J. Antonello, Adeen Flinker, Nima Mesgarani, Michael F. Bonner, Nebojsa Jojic, Jianfeng Gao
Tasks: Text classification
Code: https://github.com/csinva/weight-space-programming-autoresearch

item.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
item.description:
LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learning and constructs from machine learning literature on self-generated curricula. Furthermore, we study the extent to which the learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks, observing improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation.
Authors: Shobhita Sundaram, Cansu Sancaktar, Phillip Isola
Tasks: Agents
Code: https://github.com/ssundaram21/self-org

item.title: GameRealm: Grounding Visual Learning in Interactive Games
item.description:
Visual foundation models are central to physical intelligence, yet their development remains constrained by fragmented training datasets, inconsistent annotation quality, and limited multimodal supervision. To address these challenges, we introduce GameRealm, a large-scale, richly annotated dataset that grounds visual observations in synchronized, game-native supervision. GameRealm encompasses over 120 million RGB frames and 1,000 hours of gameplay footage across all views. Beyond its unprecedented scale, GameRealm provides rich multimodal supervision, including metric depth, camera parameters, synchronized audio, control inputs, and 3D point trajectories. Its diversity further extends to flexible view configurations, spanning single-view, stereo, multi-view, and panoramic recordings. To enable scalable acquisition across diverse game environments, we develop a unified data collection pipeline that combines human-operated interaction with agentic exploration. Extensive experiments across diverse visual learning tasks demonstrate that GameRealm consistently strengthens visual foundation models in both visual generation and geometric learning. These results establish GameRealm as a versatile and valuable data resource, unlocking new opportunities for advancing visual intelligence.
Authors: Weiguang Zhao, Yifan WANG, Ni Yang, Yating Wang, Xingyu Miao, Yankai Jiang, Mulin Yu, Tao Lu, Haoyu Guo, Junting Dong, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen
Code: https://github.com/weiguangzhao/GameRealm

item.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
item.description:
We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.
Authors: Run Luo, Kuan Zhang, Qi Deng, Yukun Chen, Zhihao Yang, Yufei Zhang, Renrong Hu, Yi Zhang, Guiyu Ma, Tianyu Fan, Longze Chen, Hao Sun, Jiaming Li, Jiaming Yang, Xiaohao Liu, Tao Tan, Minzheng Wang, Hangtian Jia, Shuai Yuan, Lvdi Wang, Xiao Liu, Chao Ma, Yuting Zou, Yinhe Zheng, Xiaobo Xia, Dawei Jiang, Shaoqing Ren
Tasks: Continual Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Robotics
Code: https://github.com/RainBowLuoCS/Gamer

item.title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
item.description:
Continuous autoregressive TTS relies on an acoustic target that enables stable next-latent modeling while preserving fine-grained acoustic details. While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual, then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel. Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel, followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel. Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh. GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively. We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step students, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame. The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.
Authors: Wenhao Guan, Jiaxin Ye, HAITAO LI, Yifan Duan, Junxi Liu, Wangjin Zhou, Lin Li, Qingyang Hong, Xie Chen
Tasks: Reinforcement Learning, Text-to-speech, Voice cloning
Code: https://github.com/VoxDance-Lab/VoxMel

item.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
item.description:
ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. For its latency and size, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and cloning fidelity. To achieve this we propose a latent MoE backbone with only 886M parameters (100M active per token) and a new audio codec, Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1), which represents 44.1 kHz audio at a 15 Hz frame rate. On the new ZTTS2-Eval benchmark, ZONOS3-Mini reaches a 6.71% macro-average WER over 55 language sets (35 clean and 20 in the wild), which is competitive with larger and slower state-of-the-art models. We release the model weights, inference, and training code.
Authors: Gabriel Clark, Sofian Mejjoute, George Close, Beren Millidge
Tasks: Audio and Speech Editing, Text-to-speech, Voice cloning
Code: https://github.com/zyphra/zonos3-mini

item.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
item.description:
Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, with a Transformer trunk shared across embodiments. A training-only embodiment-dreaming objective predicts latent representations of future visual and proprioceptive states, encouraging the shared trunk to model each embodiment's dynamics. Across 13 task-embodiment pairs spanning five tasks and six robot embodiments, including five physical robots and one simulated humanoid, cross-embodiment pretraining raises MXT+'s average normalized task progress from 0.63 to 0.80 over training from scratch. The gains are particularly pronounced under out-of-distribution conditions, where average task progress increases from 0.53 to 0.77. Ablations demonstrate the benefits of broader pretraining mixtures, modular interfaces, and embodiment dreaming, with dreaming producing more similar latent geometry across embodiments. Project page: egox-dream.github.io.
Authors: Yaru Niu, Binghong Chen, Changwei Yao, Shangtao Li, Zhenlong Fang, Revanth Krishna Senthilkumaran, Shuai Zhou, Yuemin Mao, Kalie Ching, Po-Ju Chao, Yudong Luo, Peiqi Yu, Heng Zhang, Hao Zhang, Bingqing Chen, Chen Qiu, H. Eric Tseng, Ye Yuan, Umar Iqbal, Changliu Liu, Jonathan Francis, Ding Zhao
Tasks: Robotics
Code: https://github.com/egox-dream/egox

item.title: Aligning AI Teams
item.description:
Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent teams back to single-agent alignment behavior; (3) diffusion of responsibility substantially accounts for the safety gap: agents in teams are less likely to proactively check for system-level safety failures and more likely to ignore, rationalize, or deflect responsibility for issues when they arise; (4) having a designated safety lead agent ensure system-level safety, and having a coordinator agent publish a safety specifications document are effective at restoring single-agent alignment. We also release magelab, a multi-agent LLM orchestration and experimentation framework. Our findings can help practitioners design agent teams that successfully preserve the behaviors expected of aligned individual agents.
Authors: Siddarth Srinivasan, Morgan J Matthews, Morgan Jane Matthews, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Erik Jones, Erik Jones
Tasks: Agents, Multi-Agent Systems, Recommendation Systems
Code: https://github.com/sidsrinivasan/magelab

item.title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
item.description:
CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops. The method decomposes this complex task into a chain of simple visual decisions about what to construct and what to correct. Geometric tools support precise construction, allowing the agent to focus on visual reasoning. Using the mid-sized Qwen3.8-27B model, CADMAGEDDON outperforms prior approaches, including systems based on frontier models, in reconstruction quality on all the main benchmarks. CADMAGEDDON integrates with FreeCAD, bringing its reconstructions into practitioners' existing CAD workflows. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/cadmageddon
Authors: Oleg Pavlov, Nikita Gavrilov, Soslan Kabisov, Gennadii Savrasov, Andrey Kuznetsov, Anton Konushin, Dmitrii Zhemchuzhnikov
Tasks: 3D Reconstruction, Image Understanding
Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/cadmageddon

item.title: Autonomous agents can run successful open-model organisations. Evidence from an 8-week case study
item.description:
For seven weeks, we gave Horizon, an agent based on Opus 5.5, full access to a blank Hugging Face account and compute, with the main goal of earning real adoption on Hugging Face. It used over 600 GPU-hours, autonomously created 38 models used in over 100 GitHub repositories and downloaded more than 50,000 times. Horizon runs 24/7 in Claude Code with a weekly compute budget, focuses on narrow-task multilingual models fine-tuned from mmBERT (prompt-injection guards, PII redactors, punctuation restoration, rerankers), and relies on public datasets plus synthetic data from Qwen 3.8-27B. External review finds its models often on the size/performance Pareto frontier, and we document real downstream use, including fine-tunes, pipeline integrations and independent evaluations on arXiv. We release the full agent trace.
Authors: Arthur Wuhrmann, David Schmotz, Derck Prinzhorn, Ameya Prabhu, Harry Coppock, Maksym Andriushchenko
Tasks: Agents, Auto-Research, Long-Horizon Agents
Code: https://github.com/horizon-ai-labs/agent-io-guards

item.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
item.description:
Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification. Given a boundary-representation part, stock, and material, a locally hosted, mid-sized open model proposes operations and cutting parameters for indexed three-axis machining. A geometric harness generates toolpaths, simulates material removal, and returns feedback for plan refinement. Setup planning accounts for what the available cutters can physically reach, rather than visibility alone. We evaluate the resulting programs by the fraction of the target surface area within the specified tolerance after simulated machining. With Qwen3.8-27B, MillBill outperforms frontier-model approaches that construct their own geometry and toolpath workflows on the evaluated machining tasks. Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/millbill
Authors: Gennadii Savrasov, Artem Slavin, Soslan Kabisov, Andrey Kuznetsov, Anton Konushin, Dmitrii Zhemchuzhnikov
Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/MillBill

item.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
item.description:
We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/
Authors: K2 Team, Zhengzhong Liu, Haonan Li, Xuezhe Ma, Alexander Moreno, Subham Sekhar Sahoo, Rupesh Kumar Srivastava, Mikhail Yurochkin, Hadi Abdine, Yash Akhauri, Adharsh Babu, David Bellamy, Jalaj Bhandari, Dani Bouch, Wail Bouhedja, Weili Cao, Ahmad Chamma, Po-Chun Chang, Junlin Chen, Lingjie Chen, Zhoujun Cheng, Kyle Chickering, Ryandito Diandaru, Evan Dufraisse, Chaitanya Dwivedi, Bilal El Bouardi, Desai Fan, Richard Fan, Chengqian Gao, Rifo Ahmad Genadi, Jonathan Geuter, Charles Guille-Escuret, Willis Guo, Dhawal Gupta, Seungwook Han, Tingxu Han, Shibo Hao, Besher Hassan, Guowei He, Ming Shan Hee, Joel Hestness, Yu Huang, Yuan Huang, Haolong Jia, Linghao Jin, Junu Kim, Lingjing Kong, Nurkhan Laiyk, Andrej Leban, Liqun Ma, John Maggs, Amr Mohamed, Mukhesh Narra, Omkar Pangarkar, Aldo Pareja, Khiem Pham, Varad Pimpalkhute, Nikhil Ranjan, Elizaveta Rebrova, Hector Ren, Shaurya Rohatgi, Guokan Shang, Jianshu She, Chufan Shi, Aaryamonvikram Singh, Daria Soboleva, Kartik Sreenivasan, Suqi Sun, Yuekai Sun, Bowen Tan, Liping Tang, Shengkun Tang, Muzi Tao, Mallikarjuna Tupakula, Micah Villmow, Hongyi Wang, Huijuan Wang, Renxi Wang, Yongxin Wang, Yuqi Wang, Zhenting Wang, Shicheng Wen, Yingquan Wu, Anze Xie, Andrew Xing, Matthew Yang, Shuanghai Yu, Kerem Zaman, Zenan Zhai, Hongli Zhan, Xuezhou Zhang, Anshun Asher Zheng, Zhe Zhou, Richard Zhuang, Eric P. item.title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
item.description:
Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one 360^circ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched 360^circ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at 8-46times their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.
Authors: Jiajun Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Zeyu Ren, Guangfeng Jiang, yang zhao, Hao Tang
Tasks: 3D Reconstruction, Autonomous Driving, Novel View Synthesis, Video generation, World Models
Code: https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/PanDWM

item.title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
item.description:
Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from 27.79% to 51.38% and its Calmar ratio from 0.955 to 4.043, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of 4.90 on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.
Authors: Annan Wang, Yuchen Xie, Yu Cen, Leon Liangyu Chen, Qianyu Julie Zhu, Xin Li, Tianyi Wei, Weisi Lin
Tasks: Reinforcement Learning
Code: https://github.com/allocflow/AllocFlow
